Verbs with Infinitives: Would Like to in Interrogative and Affirmative Statements
In English, there are some infinitive verbs that are always followed by other verbs such as the verb would like to.
Use the verb would like to express the desire or the intention of doing something:

You can use would like before objects or verbs; when you use it before a verb, this one goes in infinitive form. Use the following structure to make a sentence using would like:
Subject + would like + infinitive + complement.

Example:
  • I would like to understand how database software works.
  • Shannon would like to implement MySQL in the company.

• I would like to see how to code using MySQL.
  • Would you like to know how to code using MySQL?
You can use would like in interrogative structures by following the next structure: Would + Subject + Like + Infinitive + Complement + ?

• Would you like to learn a little bit more about SQL?
  • Would you like to know how to code using MySQL?
    • Note that you use would like in its interrogative form to politely offer or request something.
Would you like to give me some ideas about it?
Would you like to explain to us the difference between MySQL and SQL?
I'd like you to understand that MySQL is just a piece of software that works with that programming language.
Verbs with Infinitives: Need to in Affirmative, Negative and Interrogative Statements
In English, there are some verbs, such as would like or have, that demand the following action to be in infinitive form, one of them is need .
Use the verb need to express the necessity of something to happen: In order to make an affirmative sentence with the verb need use the following structure:
Subject + Need + Infinitive + Complement.

You can also use the verb need in negative sentences by using the following structure:
Subject + Don't/Doesn't + Need + Infinitive + Complement

Examples:
  • You don't need to use MySQL if you have to work with databases.
  • You don't need to use MySQL when you use a content management system.

You can make the interrogative form of the verb need by using the auxiliary verb do/does.
Structure:
(Wh) + Do/Does + Subject + Need + infinitive + Complement

  • Do you need to use MySQL when you use a content management system?
  • What do you need to know to implement a database?

Mr. Kapoor : Ok, class. Today, I'd like to show you why database software is necessary in our contemporary world. Let's start with the concept of database…Would you like to give me some ideas about it?
Tim : Me, sir. A database is an assembly of information containing data, such as contact information, tables, reports, files, etc.
Mr. Kapoor : You're right, Tim. Nowadays, regardless of the size of an organization, people need to handle lots of information as fast as they can, and that is why we need to use database software. Database programs, such as MySQL or PostgreSQL, help companies to manage, store and retrieve any piece of data easily.

Tim : I'm sorry, professor. Would you like to explain to us the difference between MySQL and SQL?
Mr. Kapoor : I was about to get there… To create a database, we need to use the Structure Query Language or SQL. It is mainly a declarative language that also includes some procedural elements that allow users to insert, query, update and control data into the databases. On the other hand, I'd like you to understand that MySQL is just a piece of software that works with that programming language.
Tim : Professor, do we really need to know how to work with MySQL?

Mr. Kapoor : Well, as a matter of fact, if you only work with content management systems, such as WordPress or Joomla, you don't need to worry about SQL or MySQL because, even though web-based programs and blogs need to use a SQL program to manage the databases, most web host companies provide their services with it. In general terms, you only need to know how to work with the CMS software, as it is the CMS the one in charge of dealing with the database and the SQL protocols. However, if you are programming a piece of software that needs to access the database, there you need to manage SQL and MySQL.
